papers.title: Sustained Activation of a Defensive Behavior-Related Circuit Elicits a distinct Homeostatic Sleep Response.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Compared homeostatic sleep responses in rodents after sustained wakefulness induced by gentle handling versus optogenetic stimulation of basal forebrain vGluT2 neurons, finding that vGluT2 stimulation produced a diminished recovery response with less pronounced NREM sleep time and delta power than gentle handling. Whole-brain cFos mapping showed stronger activation of stress and avoidance/defensive regions after vGluT2 stimulation.

papers.title: Automated Sleep Staging Performance Across Two Experimental Sleep Manipulation Protocols in Adolescents.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: Evaluated POPS, YASA, and combined POPS+YASA automated sleep staging against manual polysomnography in adolescents across a sleep restriction protocol and a slow-wave sleep deprivation protocol. Agreement was moderate-to-substantial overall (kappa 0.53-0.76) but declined under restricted sleep and on the slow-wave sleep deprivation night, with stage-specific degradation of Wake/N1/N2 or N3 classification.

papers.title: Real-time detection of N2 and N3 sleep from scalp and intracranial EEG
papers.summary: Developed a causal tracker that estimates N2+N3 sleep every 2 s from the preceding 10 s of scalp or intracranial EEG and tested a simulated rule for permitting stimulation. Real-time N2+N3 discrimination approached offline scoring (scalp AUC 0.953 vs 0.958), thalamic channels alone reached 0.934, and scalp plus thalamus reached 0.967, with stimulation permitted within 5 min in 63-73% of N2+N3 transitions.

papers.title: Sleep-like slow waves in wakefulness index post-stroke behavioural alterations.
papers.summary: Simultaneously recorded EEG and perceptual decision-making performance in 30 unilateral stroke patients and 27 age-matched controls, showing more frequent sleep-like slow waves in patients with some ipsilateral predominance and a significant correlation between slow-wave occurrence and accuracy and speed of perceptual reports. The authors propose these slow waves as a mechanism of post-stroke functional network dysfunction and cognitive heterogeneity.

papers.title: Detection of Spreading Depolarization with Noninvasive Electroencephalography.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: Developed and validated WAVEFRONT, a noninvasive scalp EEG biomarker of spreading depolarization based on delta-band spatiotemporal propagation, using concurrent scalp EEG and invasive subdural ECoG across three institutions in patients with TBI, SAH, or malignant hemispheric stroke. It achieved a cross-validated true positive rate of 97.3% at a 6.0% false positive rate, correlated with invasive SD counts (R2=0.7411), and showed higher SD burden on post-arrest day 3 in patients with poor neurological outcome in the I-CARE cohort.

papers.title: Optimized phase-targeted auditory stimulation reduces nocturnal spikes in childhood epilepsies
papers.summary: Compared phase-targeted auditory stimulation patterns and their effects on epileptic spikes during NREM sleep in childhood epilepsies, then tested an optimized train-based paradigm across whole nights. Exploratory work (N=10) showed isolated tones transiently increased spike rate while repetitive short-interval down-phase trains reduced it; in the proof-of-concept between-night study (N=5) spike density decreased locally in all patients.

papers.title: EEG-based deep learning estimates preterm infants' cerebral age: Contribution of slow-wave and cross-frequency coupling.
papers.summary: Developed a convolutional neural network that predicted postmenstrual age from spontaneous EEG in 165 healthy preterm infants (28-38 weeks PMA), achieving a mean absolute error of 0.75 ± 0.60 weeks with 73.9% of errors within one week. Removing low-frequency activity (<4 Hz) degraded performance and disrupting phase-amplitude coupling selectively impaired prediction before 34 weeks PMA, indicating maturation signatures are driven by slow-wave dynamics and their coupling with faster oscillations.

papers.title: How Does Sleep Deprivation Rewrite the Cognitive Function in the Hippocampus?
papers.summary: Reviews how sleep deprivation disrupts hippocampal structure and function and produces cognitive deficits, emphasizing redox-metabolic uncoupling, silenced plasticity signals, amplified neuroinflammation, and impaired synaptic efficacy, network synchrony, waste clearance, and neurogenesis. Argues for multi-modal models integrating transcriptomics, connectomics, and real-time neuromodulation to clarify cascading mechanisms.

papers.title: Sleep complaints in alexithymia reflect non-specific negative affectivity.
papers.summary: In a large in-home EEG sleep study (N=228), alexithymia was associated with worse subjective sleep quality but not with objective EEG-based sleep efficiency; the subjective associations were almost fully attenuated after adjusting for depressive symptoms or trait neuroticism, suggesting non-specific negative affectivity rather than a specific sleep alteration.

papers.title: Resting-State EEG Spectral Power in Young Adults With Generalized Anxiety Disorder and Self-Reported Habitual Short Sleep: A Case-Control Study.
papers.summary: Case-control study comparing resting-state EEG spectral power in 56 university students, 28 with generalized anxiety disorder and habitual short sleep versus 28 healthy controls. Whole-scalp estimates were directionally higher in the GAD plus short-sleep group, but no age- and sex-adjusted frequency-band comparison survived FDR correction; adjusted exploratory channel-wise effects concentrated in delta and theta over posterior and centroparietal electrodes.

papers.title: Impact of Combined Chronic Stress and REM Sleep Deprivation on Memory Function and Hippocampal BDNF Protein Content in Wistar Rats.
papers.summary: In male Wistar rats exposed for 21 days to combined chronic unpredictable mild stress and REM sleep deprivation, spatial recognition memory was impaired and body weight loss occurred, while hippocampal BDNF protein content showed a compensatory rebound to control levels rather than the suppression seen with isolated stressors.

papers.title: CK2 and DBT promote temperature compensation of the Drosophila circadian clock via distinct pathways.
papers.summary: Reduced activity of Drosophila doubletime/CK1 and casein kinase 2 (CK2) compromised temperature compensation of circadian rhythms, with genetic analyses indicating distinct but additive pathways. DBT acts through the per Short phosphorylation cluster and PER Ser47 phosphodegron, whereas CK2 acts through a phosphocluster in TIM and PER Ser45; simultaneous disruption caused hyperphosphorylated PER accumulation and impaired PER clearance from pacemaker neuron nuclei.

papers.title: Loss of PEA-15 Alters ERK/MAPK Signaling and Circadian Function in the Suprachiasmatic Nucleus.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Using PEA-15 knockout mice, the authors show that loss of the scaffold protein PEA-15 reduces both clock-gated and light-evoked ERK activation in the suprachiasmatic nucleus, shortens the free-running period under constant darkness, and blunts phase-delay responses to light while accelerating entrainment to phase-advancing light. The findings identify PEA-15 as a regulator of SCN circadian timing and photic entrainment via ERK/MAPK signaling.

papers.title: Modeling circadian rhythm splitting under chronic light and the asymmetric transition kinetics between lighting conditions
papers.summary: The authors build a two-lobe biophysical model of the SCN using interacting ventral core and dorsal shell Kuramoto oscillator populations to explain circadian rhythm splitting under chronic light. They propose that light-induced shifts in GABAergic excitation/inhibition balance, driven by chloride cotransporter expression changes, flip ipsilateral and contralateral coupling signs so that left and right shell populations oscillate in antiphase, reproducing splitting, unilateral lesion effects, and experimental data.

papers.title: Rest-activity rhythm fragmentation, functional limitation, and mortality in adults with arthritis: A nationally representative cohort study.
papers.summary: In 7,920 NHANES adults with wrist accelerometry, arthritis was associated with more fragmented rest-activity rhythms and lower peak daytime activity, with functional limitation accounting for most of the fragmentation difference; higher intradaily variability was associated with all-cause mortality, including within the arthritis subgroup.

papers.title: Chronotherapy leveraging dietary context overcomes circadian rhythm influence on cancer cell response to PPAR antagonists.
papers.summary: Using 2D and 3D colorectal cancer models and tumor-bearing mice, this study found that nutrient-defined feeding-fasting media abolished circadian time-dependent variability in PPAR antagonist sensitivity, and that fed-state dosing of a PPAR-γ antagonist prolonged survival and reduced hepatotoxicity, with Bmal1-silenced cells indicating feeding-fasting rhythms rather than tumor-intrinsic clocks govern drug sensitivity.

papers.title: Multi-Modal Wearable and Biological Data Integration Reveals Physiological Signatures of Weight Variation in Overweight and Obese Adults: An AI4Food Machine Learning Study
papers.summary: In a 30-day crossover intervention with 93 overweight or obese adults, the AI4Food study integrated wearable, glucose sensor, nutritional, and gut microbiome data and applied clustering, association analysis, and machine learning to identify physiological correlates of weight variation. Nocturnal respiratory rate and skin temperature were significantly associated with weight change, Random Forest models reached mean accuracies of 64.3% for thermoregulation and 61.7% for glucose phenotype prediction, and microbiome composition remained nearly stable.

papers.title: Enlightening pregnancy as a potential pathway to protect maternal circadian functioning and postpartum mood.
papers.summary: This longitudinal study followed women from late pregnancy to one month postpartum using wrist actigraphy and questionnaires to characterize circadian function, phase, preference, light exposure, and mood. The postpartum transition showed reduced circadian function index and mean light exposure without a phase shift; prenatal circadian function and eveningness predicted postpartum depressive symptoms and lower postpartum circadian function, identifying eveningness as a vulnerability factor.

papers.title: Electroencephalography-based machine learning models for hyperacute detection of large vessel occlusion stroke.
papers.summary: Using single 2-3 minute 8-electrode EEG recordings from 336 patients with suspected stroke, EEG-based machine learning models detected anterior circulation large vessel occlusion with moderately high accuracy, with Naive Bayes achieving an AUC of 0.85, 69% sensitivity, and 86% specificity.

papers.title: Disrupted cortical signatures of response inhibition in Parkinson's disease revealed by TMS-EEG.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: Using TMS-EEG during a Go/NoGo task in 36 Parkinson's disease patients (18 with L-DOPA-induced dyskinesias) and 20 healthy volunteers, this study found that task-dependent SMA-M1 theta/gamma connectivity and NoGo N100 responses present in controls were absent in PD patients, especially those with dyskinesias, and SMA-M1 gamma connectivity correlated with motor performance and clinical severity.

papers.title: Squalamine prevents motor and non-motor symptoms in the paraquat and lectin rat model of the body-first subtype of Parkinson's disease.
papers.summary: Tested whether the paraquat and lectin (P+L) rat model recapitulates non-motor features of body-first Parkinson's disease and whether oral squalamine prevents pathology and symptoms. P+L rats showed gastrointestinal dysmotility and sleep abnormalities, and 30 days of squalamine prevented motor deficits, gastrointestinal dysmotility, and sleep abnormalities while reducing phospho-S129-alpha-synuclein pathology and nigrostriatal neurodegeneration.

papers.title: Pathophysiology of REM sleep behaviour disorder.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes post-mortem histology, neuroimaging, and pharmacological evidence to describe mechanisms of altered REM sleep regulation in REM sleep behaviour disorder (RBD) and its role as a prodromal marker of α-synucleinopathies. It discusses biomarkers and mechanisms of phenoconversion to α-synucleinopathies from large longitudinal cohorts and proposes future research directions.

papers.title: Integrative Multi-Omics Reveals Differential Mechanisms of Four TCM Formulations in Treating Insomnia via Syndrome-Compound-Metabolite Association Networks.
papers.summary: Combining UHPLC-Orbitrap-MS/MS constituent profiling, a meta-analysis of 62 RCTs, and multi-omics in a sleep-deprivation mouse model, this study showed four TCM insomnia formulations share anti-inflammatory and anti-ferroptosis effects and reversal of Alistipes and 39 serum metabolites but display syndrome-associated differences in microbiota-metabolite networks.

papers.title: Strategies to establish a biologically defined Parkinson's disease cohort prior to the onset of clinically significant motor symptoms.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: The Parkinson's Precision Medicine Initiative evaluated recruitment strategies (polysomnogram-confirmed RBD, central hyposmia testing, and dream enactment behavior) to enroll individuals before clinically significant motor symptoms. CSFaSynSAA positivity was highest in RBD+Hyposmia (94%) and Hyposmia+DEB (85%) versus RBD-Hyposmia (40%) and Hyposmia-DEB (55%), revealing biomarker and multi-domain clinical heterogeneity among CSFaSynSAA-positive individuals presymptomatically.

papers.title: Effect of Intraoperative Subanesthetic-Dose Esketamine on Postoperative Hydromorphone Consumption After Total Hip Arthroplasty: A Randomized Double-Blind Placebo-Controlled Trial.
papers.summary: In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of 128 total hip arthroplasty patients, intraoperative subanesthetic-dose esketamine reduced first 24-h hydromorphone consumption (2.24 vs 3.20 mg, P<0.001) and 48-h consumption, with lower NRS pain scores at 6 and 24 h and lower postoperative sleep disturbance incidence (26.6% vs 54.7%).

papers.title: Sleep components, depressive subdomains and quality of life in Parkinson's disease: A cross-sectional exploratory analysis.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional exploratory analysis of 55 hospitalized Parkinson's disease patients found that the HAMD total depressive symptom score was the only significant independent correlate of both physical and mental quality of life, while PSQI total score was not; exploratory analyses suggested sleep components linked to QoL indirectly through distinct depressive subdimensions (Retardation, Anxiety/Somatization).

papers.title: Circadian blood pressure dipping patterns, hypertension, and cortisol metabolism across the weight spectrum.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 426 participants undergoing 24-h ambulatory blood pressure monitoring, cortisol metabolism markers did not differ significantly between dippers and nondippers, but higher 24-h urinary cortisol/cortisone ratio was associated with higher 24-h mean systolic BP among nondippers with BMI 18.5-29.9 kg/m2.

papers.title: Ecological Momentary Interventions (EMIs) and Just-in-Time Adaptive Interventions (JITAIs) for sleep and circadian health: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 11 RCTs found that ecological momentary and just-in-time adaptive interventions significantly improved sleep efficiency, insomnia severity, dysfunctional sleep beliefs, and depressive symptoms, while no included studies reported circadian outcomes.

papers.title: Serum metabolic alterations associated with Chaihu-Longgu-Muli decoction in adolescents with insomnia: An exploratory untargeted metabolomics study.
papers.summary: In an exploratory untargeted metabolomics study of 30 adolescents with chronic insomnia receiving Chaihu-Longgu-Muli decoction, 30 receiving CBT, and 10 healthy controls, both interventions improved PSQI, SAS, and SDS scores, and CLMD treatment was associated with serum metabolite shifts toward control levels in sphingolipid and related pathways.

papers.title: Developmental trajectories of pain empathy: evidence from drift diffusion modeling and EEG time-frequency analysis.
papers.summary: Used hierarchical drift-diffusion modeling and EEG time-frequency analysis in 120 children, adolescents, and adults performing attention-to-pain-cue tasks to characterize developmental trajectories of pain empathy. Children showed lower drift rates, wider decision boundaries, and longer non-decision times, with reduced alpha- and beta-band ERD differentiation between painful and non-painful stimuli when pain cues were task-irrelevant.

papers.title: Volume status as a potential state-dependent modifier of obstructive sleep apnea severity in chronic kidney disease and dialysis: a narrative review.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on whether volume status acts as a state-dependent modifier of obstructive sleep apnea severity in chronic kidney disease and dialysis. It concludes that fluid overload and regional fluid measures are associated with OSA severity mainly in small hemodialysis studies, but findings do not establish a reproducible volume-sensitive OSA phenotype or justify changes to sleep-study timing, PAP management, or upper-airway treatment selection.

papers.title: Effects of environmental enrichments applied to pasture areas on free-range laying hens: 2. Pasture use, behaviour and welfare.
papers.summary: In a study of 900 free-range laying hens, object enrichment increased use of the inner pasture zone (p < 0.01), but total pasture use, behaviour, and welfare indicators did not differ among enrichment treatments. Age affected behaviour and welfare, with older hens showing more feeding, drinking, walking, foraging, and deteriorated feather and footpad condition.

papers.title: Identification and validation of circadian rhythm-related diagnostic biomarkers for endometriosis through integrating machine learning and single-cell analysis.
papers.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
papers.summary: Using WGCNA, four machine learning algorithms, three independent GEO validation cohorts, immune infiltration analyses, and single-cell RNA-seq, this study identified SMC2, SUV39H2, and TIMELESS as candidate circadian rhythm-related diagnostic biomarkers for endometriosis with favorable diagnostic performance. Single-cell analyses further revealed increased mesenchymal cells and altered BMP, CHEMERIN, and GRN signaling in endometriosis samples.

papers.title: Rapidly progressive cognitive decline and drug-induced encephalopathy secondary to teprotumumab for thyroid eye disease: a case report and narrative literature review.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 56-year-old Han-Chinese man with Graves' disease and thyroid eye disease who developed rapidly progressive encephalopathy with cognitive and behavioral dysfunction 20 days after the third teprotumumab infusion, with interictal epileptiform discharges on video-EEG and a Naranjo score of 6. The patient recovered after therapeutic plasma exchange and symptomatic management; a narrative review of all published cases proposes a three-hit pathogenic hypothesis involving impaired IGF-1R neurotrophic signaling, thyroid autoimmunity, and metabolic disturbance.

papers.title: A Kampo medicine, kamishoyosan, ameliorates menstruation-associated symptoms in patients with premenstrual syndrome: An exploratory open-label, randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: In this exploratory open-label randomized controlled trial of 50 patients, kamishoyosan administered over three menstrual cycles significantly ameliorated the primary endpoint of premenstrual Menstrual Distress Questionnaire total score and reduced several symptom subscales, with headache as the only related adverse event.

papers.title: Effects of environmental enrichments applied to pasture areas on free-range laying hens: 1. Performance and egg quality.
papers.summary: In 900 Lohmann Brown hens, environmental enrichment did not affect hen-day egg production but significantly decreased albumen index and affected dirty egg ratio and shell thickness (p < 0.01), while object enrichment improved some albumen and shell quality traits. Age significantly influenced all performance and egg quality traits (p < 0.05).

papers.title: Organised streaming of cerebrospinal fluid in the human third ventricle
papers.summary: Used transient CFD simulations of the human third ventricle to show that increasing peak aqueduct Reynolds number, via stroke volume and frequency combinations, transitions flow from reversible oscillation to preferential streaming pathways across the aqueduct. The dimensionless streaming ratio followed a rational saturation relation SR ~ ReAq,peak/(C + ReAq,peak), bounding the relative contribution of residual inter-ventricular streaming.

papers.title: Neuromodulatory effects of audio-proprio-phonatory reinforcement training on subjective tinnitus, a HD-EEG study protocol.
papers.summary: This protocol describes a prospective, controlled, randomized study to evaluate audio-proprio-phonatory reinforcement training for chronic subjective tinnitus in 56 patients, with the Tinnitus Handicap Inventory as the primary endpoint and HD-EEG to assess changes in brain activity.

papers.title: "It Just Puts You Out!" 'Tranq Sleep,' Sensory Discernment, and the Experience of Consuming Xylazine-Adulterated Fentanyl in Rural North Carolina.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This qualitative study conducted 25 semi-structured interviews with fentanyl consumers in rural west-central North Carolina to examine how they detect, understand, and respond to xylazine adulteration, describing sensory discernment strategies and a distinctive involuntary sedation termed 'tranq sleep.' It provides among the first qualitative descriptions of xylazine exposure in a rural fentanyl market and underscores the need for tailored harm reduction responses.

papers.title: Lineage-specific histories rather than shared drivers shape olfactory evolution in New World monkeys
papers.summary: Using genomic, anatomical, and ecological data from 80 New World monkey species, this study found that ecological and sensory variables explain little variation in olfactory receptor repertoires; instead, lineage-specific histories shaped olfactory evolution, with convergent reductions in repertoire size arising through distinct genomic mechanisms and partial decoupling between receptor repertoire size and olfactory bulb volume within lineages.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
